facts.statement: The name Dermodactylus means "skin finger" because its wings were skin membranes supported by the ring fingers.
facts.quote: Dermodactylus (meaning "skin finger", from Greek derma and daktylos, in reference to pterosaur wings being skin membranes supported by the ring fingers)

facts.statement: The genus is known from a single partial bone found in the hand.
facts.quote: It is based on a single partial bone, from the hand.

facts.statement: The type specimen, a distal right fourth metacarpal, was found by Samuel Wendell Williston at Como Bluff, Wyoming, in 1878.
facts.quote: Dermodactylus is based on a single distal right fourth metacarpal found by Samuel Wendell Williston at Como Bluff, Wyoming in 1878

facts.statement: When described, this bone was the oldest known, recognized, and described pterosaur remains from North America.
facts.quote: This bone constituted at the time the oldest pterosaur remains found, recognized, and described from North America.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh originally named the species Pterodactylus montanus.
facts.quote: Othniel Charles Marsh first named it as a species of Pterodactylus: P. montanus

facts.statement: The exact placement of Dermodactylus within Pterosauria is uncertain, though it is known to be a pterodactyloid.
facts.quote: Its place within the Pterosauria is uncertain, beyond the Pterodactyloidea.

facts.statement: Due to the meagerness of the fossil material, Dermodactylus is now regarded as a dubious pterodactyloid.
facts.quote: and so it is now regarded as a dubious pterodactyloid.

facts.statement: Dermodactylus lived during the Upper Jurassic (Kimmeridgian-Tithonian) in the Morrison Formation of Wyoming, United States.
facts.quote: from the Kimmeridgian-Tithonian-age Upper Jurassic Morrison Formation of Wyoming, United States.

facts.statement: John Foster estimated the weight of Dermodactylus at 3.3 kg.
facts.quote: John Foster estimates its weight at 3.3 kg.

facts.statement: Dermodactylus was likely a small aerial carnivore.
facts.quote: It would probably have been a small aerial carnivore.

facts.statement: Dermodactylus was probably about 60 cm long with a wingspan of 1 meter, making it a very small pterosaur.
facts.quote: Probablemente medía 60 cm de largo y 1 m de envergadura, un pterodáctilo bastante pequeño.

facts.statement: Dermodactylus had a beak with teeth and likely used them to hunt insects.
facts.quote: Su hocico tenía dientes y probablemente con ellos cazaba insectos.

facts.statement: Unlike other pterodactyloids, Dermodactylus probably did not live on cliffs or hunt fish.
facts.quote: Probablemente no vivía en acantilados ni cazaba peces, a diferencia de otros pterodactiloideos.
